resources.string: Advanced
Settings with a cost worth knowing about. The defaults are what most devices should keep.
Uncloak CNAME trackers
Inspect answers, not just questions

Some trackers are served under a name belonging to the site you are on — metrics.example.com — which then resolves onto the tracker\'s real domain. The question looks first-party, so nothing on a blocklist can match it. Only the answer names the tracker. This checks the answer.

The cost: every answer that arrives is parsed and each name in its chain is checked against the index — up to eight extra lookups for a lookup that would otherwise have been one. Blocked-tracker rows in the log will name the tracker rather than the site\'s own subdomain, and the query counters count evaluations rather than lookups.
On — answers are being checked.
Off — only the queried name is checked.
Unavailable: the control page is not mapped, so this switch has nothing to write to.
Could not write the setting. Nothing changed.
Who per-app policy applies to
Checking…

Policy is stored per app, not per profile. The resolver looks it up by app ID and never sees which user asked, so blocking or exempting an app here does the same for that app in every profile on this device.
This copy of Nullroute runs as user %1$d.
This is a work profile. Changes made here reach the device owner\'s apps too.
No other user has resolved anything yet, so nothing else is affected right now.
Other users seen in the query log: %1$s. Their copies of the same app share this policy.
The query log is off or empty, so other profiles cannot be listed — which is not evidence that none exist.
What this screen cannot prove

These switches write to the control page. The resolver inside netd is what acts on them, and a build whose resolver patch was applied without the CNAME hunk will read the byte and ignore it. There is no probe for that yet, so treat the switch as a request rather than as a report.
